source.note: PROVENANCE, read this before trusting any number derived from it. The per-turn usage blocks below are HAND-COMPUTED. No provider produced them and no HTTP traffic was captured. They are what an explicit-breakpoint provider with a 1024-token minimum WOULD report given this fixture's own declared byte counts, evaluated with the engine's own bytes/4 estimator: turn 0 caches nothing because the whole prefix is 560 tokens and below the minimum; turn 1 writes the full 1076-token prefix and reads nothing; every later turn reads back what the previous turn wrote and writes only the delta. Because the expectation and the prediction come from the same token estimator, an arithmetic-accuracy run over this fixture is a SELF-CONSISTENCY CHECK: it catches an attribution, carry or prefix-region bug, and it cannot validate the vendor cache model or establish section 20's 5-percent band, which is defined against counts providers actually reported.

stable.system: You are a coding assistant operating inside a repository. Read files before editing them. Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request. Never invent an API. When a build or test command exists, run it before reporting success. Explain a decision only when the decision is not obvious from the diff. Keep responses short. This block is deliberately long enough to sit above a provider minimum cacheable prefix on its own.
